biography.plain_text: Mustafa Vehbi Koç was a third-generation Turkish industrialist who chaired Koç Holding from 2003 until his death in 2016. He sharpened the family conglomerate around energy, automotive, consumer-durable and financial businesses, while overseeing major acquisitions including Tüpraş and Yapı Kredi. His tenure also began the group's largest period of organic investment.

long_biography.plain_text:
Soon after becoming chairman of Koç Holding in 2003, Mustafa Vehbi Koç narrowed the inherited conglomerate toward sectors where it could lead and reach consumers. The strategy produced a defining burst of dealmaking in 2005: Koç acquired control of Yapı Kredi and won the bid for Tüpraş, deepening the group's positions in banking and energy. He then launched its largest organic-investment period and pressed for international growth, stronger brands and technology.

Koç had entered the group at Tofaş after studying business administration, then advanced through sales and divisional leadership before joining the board. As the third generation of the founding family, he inherited both ownership and responsibility, but his thirteen-year chairmanship was operational rather than ceremonial. He also served Turkish business institutions and the Vehbi Koç Foundation. His sudden death at 55 ended a tenure that had moved the group into the ranks of the world's largest companies.
